THE SYSTEM SHALL import it only as ...'); the system performs no such import, so the criterion is vacuous at the caller level and its shape obligation is already met and drift-tested.
The guard-override JSONL is the guard's LIVE consumption ledger (guard-git.mjs:66), not a dormant record awaiting migration. Nothing in the repo needs those 5 entries in the governance journal.

The one real legacy-import path (migrate-backlog-state.mjs) is one-time and already executed -- backlog/transitions.ndjson exists, so applyBacklogMigration:99 refuses forever. Wiring a producer into a dead path is a test-only path with extra steps.

That path also refuses authority-bearing legacy records (line 47) instead of importing them as observations, and already disclaims closure via its own transition schema -- a legacy-import-observation there would be a duplicate record of the same fact.
The governing design doc sec.5/sec.6 already ruled this a PO amendment decision, deliberately untaken, and named building it as the reverted cc43a182 anti-pattern.
